text: {"findings":[{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"No experiment plan; full rollout with dashboard monitoring","detail":"The proposal has no randomization, control group, duration, MDE, or power analysis. Rolling out to all markets and watching a dashboard cannot attribute any change in acceptance rate to the incentive.","evidence_quote":"None. We will roll out to all markets and monitor the dashboard.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Design a randomized test (e.g., zone- or time-block-level randomization with spillover controls) running at least 14 days, with a stated MDE and power calculation, before any broad rollout."},{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Driver pay change without required review","detail":"A surge incentive changes driver compensation, which is a policy-controlled pay area. The Reviews section says 'None', so no pay/compensation review is recorded.","evidence_quote":"## Reviews And Dependencies\nNone.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Obtain and record the required pay/compensation policy review (and legal/finance sign-off as applicable) before launch."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Required guardrails for pay incentive absent","detail":"An incentive changes driver pay behavior but there are no guardrails on incentive cost or spend, delivery time/lateness, order cancellations, or driver earnings/supply impact. The only guardrail listed is neighboring-zone acceptance, which is vague.","evidence_quote":"Driver Acceptance Rate in neighboring zones: should not drop.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as incentive cost per order, on-time delivery rate, order cancellation rate, unassigned order rate, and cost per incremental delivery, each with thresholds."},{"type":"NO_BASELINE_TARGET","title":"Guardrail lacks numeric threshold; success metric misaligned with problem","detail":"The guardrail has no baseline or numeric threshold ('should not drop'). The success metric also does not measure the stated problem of unassigned orders from short supply, and no baseline is given for unassigned orders.","evidence_quote":"Driver Acceptance Rate in neighboring zones: should not drop.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Define numeric guardrail thresholds with baselines, and add a success metric tied to the problem (e.g., unassigned order rate in evening peak, with baseline, target, and timeframe)."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Ambiguous scope of 'peak hours' and neighboring zones","detail":"The 'peak hours' window and 'neighboring zones' are not defined, so the success and guardrail metrics are ambiguous and cannot be measured consistently. The proposal also names 'Evening' in the title but 'peak hours' in the body.","evidence_quote":"Launch a surge incentive during peak hours across all markets","citations":[],"recommendation":"Define peak-hour windows and neighboring-zone membership precisely, and use canonical glossary definitions for Driver Acceptance Rate."}]}
